extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, independent/community reporters, news bloggers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for evaluating and producing news in a networked, grassroots context emphasizing transparency, audience collaboration, and iterative reporting rather than traditional gatekeeping. Useful for reporters, editors, and independent news projects adapting news values for online communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sourced, citable, transparent reporting — the work should be verifiable by readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show primary sources and documentation; make fact-check trails visible. Examples: annotated stories with primary documents and visible provenance; avoid hiding sources or methods. Scoring note: higher value when claims can be independently checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linkability
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers can follow the trail to primary sources; the story trusts the reader to follow links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to original documents, data, and prior reporting. Test to apply: 'Does this story trust the reader to follow links?' Linkability supports verifiability and enables readers to inspect evidence themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversational
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting incorporates comments, corrections, and audience input — treats audience as collaborators rather than passive recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate reader corrections and expertise in reporting (crowdsourced reporting, verified). Evaluate whether mechanisms exist for conversation (comments, correction logs) and whether the reporter uses audience expertise as input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update-able
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are iterative and live-updated rather than static snapshots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use live updating coverage and clear update histories. Test to apply: 'Are we open to correction in real time?' Value increases when updates are transparent and dated, and when new information is integrated promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche-relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest value is for communities directly affected — hyper-local or specialized reporting that serves a specific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that matters to an affected community; support specialized hyper-local beats. Crowdsourced and community-driven reporting can raise value when it addresses niche needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provenance disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose who produced the piece and why — provide meta-information about how a story was produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include bylines, funding/conflict disclosures, methodological notes and explanation of sources/approach. Test to apply: 'Have we shown our work?' This increases trust and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust-the-reader test
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does this story trust the reader to follow links?" — a quick diagnostic for linkability/transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this question to check whether the article surfaces primary materials and provides context rather than hiding sourcing behind claims. Failing this test indicates low linkability/verifiability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show-your-work test
rubrics_metrics.description: "Have we shown our work?" — assesses whether reporting exposes methods, sources, and reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the answer is no, provide more documentation, source citation, and methodological explanation. Showing work strengthens verifiability and provenance disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness-to-correction test
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are we open to correction in real time?" — assesses systems for acknowledging and incorporating fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for correction logs, visible updates and mechanisms for reader feedback. High scoring outlets accept and publish corrections transparently and update stories iteratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-as-expertise test
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are we using audience expertise as input?" — evaluates whether reporting solicits and uses community knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether reporting processes invite tips, local knowledge, or verification from readers and whether that input is vetted and credited. Crowdsourced reporting that is verified rates highly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on official sources (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not default to official sources as the sole or primary authority; this limits perspectives and can miss local/community context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek diverse sources including affected community members, primary documents, and independent verification. Over-reliance on officials reduces verifiability and niche-relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid closed publishing models that hide errors (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed workflows and opaque editorial processes that hide how a story was produced reduce trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer open publishing practices: publish drafts, corrections, provenance details, and update histories. Closed models impede conversational orientation and update-ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process-oriented newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness should be judged as much by process attributes — transparency, verifiability, openness — as by content attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a story, consider both what is reported and how it was reported (sources, disclosure, update practices, audience engagement). Apply process metrics (the principles above) alongside traditional content judgments.
